Assuming there are 10 producers in the food chain, and each producer transfers 10% of the energy to the Arctic fox, the total energy transferred to the Arctic fox would be 10% of the total energy produced by all producers.

If the total energy produced by all producers is 100 kilojoules, then the energy transferred to the Arctic fox would be 10 kilojoules.

If the Arctic fox increases the energy by 2 kilojoules, then the total energy in the food chain would be 12 kilojoules.

Therefore, the minimum amount of energy that all producers in the food chain need to contain in total is 12 kilojoules.
